passages.title: 1. The Three-Way Botanical Phrase Crib Paradigm (`f88v.4` Label <-> `f105r.1-8` Chained Recipes <-> `f114v.36-38` Recipe)
passages.description: Demonstrates the 2-word botanical label `<f88v.4,@Lf> otar . arody` (`18.47` rarity bits) recurring across three distinct syntactic environments with predictable positional allography: (a) standalone plant label `otar . arody` (`o-` nominal + `t` gallows), (b) paragraph-initial recipe header `<f105r.6,@P0> <%>par . arody` (top-line `p` gallows, chained to `<f105r.1-5>` via shared `L.` star), and (c) interior line-final clause closer `<f114v.37,+P0> ... chey . tar . arody <$>` (unprefixed `t` gallows).

passages.title: 2. Same-Star Chained Recipe Pairs: Parallel Template Cloning (`f115r:P5->P6`) & Tail-to-Head Catenation (`f111r:P3->P4`)
passages.description: Demonstrates why the rubricator repeated the same marginal star (`L. -> L.`) on 10 pairs in Quire 20: on `f115r:P5->P6`, the two recipes clone the exact 4-slot opening sequence (`tch -> qokch -> qotch -> l-pch/polch`); on `f111r:P3->P4`, the closing words of P3 (`lkeedy . lkedar . okeedy`) catenate directly into the opening clause of P4 (`<%>pchedar . oteeol . lkeedain . okeam`).

passages.title: 3. The Rosettes-Anchored Herbal Treatise (`f48v`, Lines 7-11)
passages.description: Paragraph 2 of Herbal folio `f48v` (`Hand 1, Language A`), where line `<f48v.9,+P0>` splits across the central flower stalk (`<->`) and cites the exact 2-word Cosmological Rosettes label `<fRos.45,+L0> otchdy . otoldy` (`19.53` rarity bits) followed two words later by `otedy` (`<fRos.72> otedain . otedy`).

passages.title: 4. The First Crimson-Star Triad (`D -> L_1 -> L_2`) on `f103r` (Paragraphs 1-3, Lines 1-11)
passages.description: Illustrates the 3-part functional division of the Crimson-Star (`D -> L -> L`) triads on `f103r`: Slot 1 (`★D`, Master Recipe) introduces the core preparation; Slot 2 (`★L`, First Follower) expands nominal/ingredient quantities (`-aiin`); Slot 3 (`★L`, Second Follower) executes high-density verbal actions (`-edy/-dy`).
